answer: Anchor every identity to a name it alone controls: registration publishes a signed DNS record and the host must serve a fresh nonce, re-proving the name each epoch or the seat slides to its nadir. Names are globally unique, so k clones need k, and weight decays geometrically for each extra name under one apex, hitting zero past a small cap, so a farm's lotus of subdomains on one cheap domain earns less per head than scattered registrations. A voyage of the nonce through three independent resolvers audits that the name is live, not parked. If a renewal lapses, the bond burns.
